title: X-ray a femur phantom AP: hip end toward the cathode, centred, R marker in the field
instruction: AP right femur. The cream strip along the x-ray table's edge stands for the tube housing; its two ends are marked - and +. Lay the femur phantom on the table for an AP projection, set the way a radiographer positions it for this tube, centred on the black cross and wholly inside the yellow light field. Then put the correct side marker (red R, blue L) inside the light field without covering the bone, and let go of everything.
context: Radiographers position long bones for the anode heel effect: the x-ray beam is noticeably stronger at the tube's cathode end than at its anode end, so the thick end of a long part goes under the cathode to even out the density along the image (Bontrager and Lampignano, Textbook of Radiographic Positioning). For an AP femur the hip end goes toward the cathode, the femur lies along the tube's cathode-anode axis, centred to the central ray inside the collimated light field, and a side marker (R for a right limb) goes in the field, off the anatomy. A femur set the wrong way round gives a pale hip and a dark knee; a missing or wrong marker can mean a repeat. Here the tube is a labelled housing strip beside the table, and the phantom starts crosswise: it must be turned a quarter turn, and only the heel-effect rule says which way.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and stands for the room's floor. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A bench mock-up of a radiography room at about 40% scale; everything except the phantom and the two markers is fixed to the table. (1) X-ray table: a dark grey wooden slab, 260 mm (x) by 160 mm (y), 10 mm thick, spanning x 17.0-43.0 cm and y -8.0 to +8.0 cm; its long axis runs along x. (2) Light field: a pale yellow painted rectangle, 210 mm (x) by 130 mm (y), 0.5 mm of paint on the table top at x 19.5-40.5 cm, y -6.5 to +6.5 cm: the collimated field. (3) Central-ray cross: two black painted lines, each 60 mm long and 2 mm wide, flush with the field, one along x and one along y, crossing at x 30.0 cm, y 0. (4) Tube housing strip: a cream painted wooden bar, 260 mm (x) by 20 mm (y), 30 mm tall (its top 20 mm above the x-ray table's top), standing against the x-ray table's right-hand (-y) edge at y -10.0 to -8.0 cm, x 17.0-43.0 cm. It stands for the x-ray tube's housing, whose cathode-anode axis runs along the table. On its top at the far end (x 38.5-42.5 cm) a black plastic plate, 40 x 20 x 1 mm, with a white painted minus sign (a 24 x 5 mm bar along x) marks the cathode end; at the near end (x 17.5-21.5 cm) a red plastic plate of the same size with a white painted plus sign (24 x 5 mm and 5 x 16 mm bars) marks the anode end. (5) Side cart: a white plastic slab, 80 mm (x) by 220 mm (y), 10 mm thick, at x 23.0-31.0 cm, y -43.0 to -21.0 cm. (6) Femur phantom, loose: a rigid bone-white right-femur phantom (plastic shell, foam core), 180 mm long and 40 mm wide all along, 0.22 kg. Its height steps up from the knee end to the hip end: a 60 mm knee section 24 mm tall, a 70 mm shaft 36 mm tall and a 30 mm hip section 48 mm tall, the hip end capped by a round femoral head (an upright cylinder 40 mm across and 48 mm tall, centred 20 mm in from the phantom's hip end, on the hip section's outer face, so it sticks out 20 mm beyond the boxes). From above the hip end is round and the knee end square, with two grey painted condyles (20 x 14 mm each, side by side) on its top. Its flat underside is the posterior face, its stepped top the anterior face; its centre of mass is 16 mm from mid-length toward the hip end. It lies flat on the cart, crosswise to the table (its length along y), centred at x 27.0 cm, y -32.0 cm, hip end toward +y (toward the table). (7) Marker tray: a grey plastic slab, 50 mm (x) by 100 mm (y), 10 mm thick, at x 22.5-27.5 cm, y +27.0 to +37.0 cm. (8) Two side markers, loose: plastic blocks that each stand for a lead letter marker, 24 x 24 x 16 mm, 30 g, plain faces, lying flat on the tray at x 25.0 cm: the red R marker at y +30.0 cm and the blue L marker at y +34.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the phantom and the markers and both grippers (in a real trial: a ruler and a photo from above). 'Released': each gripper's fingers at least 5 mm from the object (a gripper's fingers are taken as everything within reach of a pad's outer corner around the 38 mm stretch back from the point between its pad tips: half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, 13.5 mm across, up to 57 mm when fully open). 'Still': its centre moved under 1.5 mm in each of the last two 0.5 s and its heading changed under 2 degrees over the last 1 s. 'Flat on the table': the phantom's lowest point within 3 mm of the light field's top and its anterior (stepped) face up, tilted under 5 degrees. 'Aligned': its length within 10 degrees of the table's long axis (x, the tube's cathode-anode axis) seen from above. 'In the field': its whole outline seen from above inside the light field. 'Centred': its centre (half-way along its length) within 15 mm of the cross. 'Hip toward the cathode': its round hip end toward the minus end of the strip (+x). 'Marker OK': the R marker released and still, lying flat (tilted under 10 degrees, either face up, its lowest point within 3 mm of the field's top), its centre inside the light field and its outline at least 5 mm clear of the phantom's outline seen from above; and the L marker's centre not inside the light field. Score 0 if the phantom touched the floor (any point of it lower than 5 mm above the station table top, that is below the tops of the cart, the x-ray table and the tray) at any step of the trial (latched: picking it up again does not undo it), or if it is not released, not still, not flat on the table (held, propped on a marker, on its side, upside down, standing on an end, on the cart or on the strip), not aligned (crosswise or diagonal) or not wholly in the field. Otherwise: 0.25 if its hip end is toward the anode (plus end), whatever its centring and the markers; with the hip end toward the cathode, 0.5 if its centre is more than 15 mm from the cross (this always needs some offset across the table: the 210 mm field leaves the 180 mm phantom at most 15 mm of play along x, the 130 mm field leaves it 45 mm across), 0.75 if centred but the marker condition fails (no marker in the field, the R marker on the bone, outside the field, under 5 mm from the bone, tilted, still held or moving, or the L marker in the field), 1.0 if centred and the marker condition holds (success, held 1 s). The R marker may lie on either side of the bone. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0; every end state maps to exactly one.
fidelity: The patient is a rigid femur phantom about 40% of real size, stepped rather than smoothly tapered; the tube is a labelled housing strip beside the table instead of an overhead tube, the light field is painted on, and no image is taken. The markers are plain red (R) and blue (L) blocks. What the radiographer must get right, the thick end toward the cathode, the part centred on the central ray inside the field and the correct marker in the field off the bone, is kept exactly.
reset_notes: Put the femur phantom back on the white side cart, lying flat with its length along y, centred at x 27.0 cm, y -32.0 cm, its round hip end toward +y (toward the table) and its stepped anterior face up. Put the red R marker on the grey tray at x 25.0 cm, y +30.0 cm and the blue L marker at x 25.0 cm, y +34.0 cm, lying flat. Nothing is consumed; everything else is fixed.
